title: .NET Standard
sub: An API contract, not a runtime. And why 2.1 matters
cards/0/body:
By 2016 .NET came in several flavors: Framework, Core, Mono, Xamarin, Unity, UWP. Each had its own set of APIs.

Library authors did not know what to target. Build a separate DLL for each one?
cards/1/title: A standard is a list, not a program
cards/1/body:
.NET Standard is a list of APIs a platform must provide. It runs nothing by itself.

Think of a power outlet standard: it does not supply electricity, but any device with the right plug fits any outlet that follows the standard.

A library built for netstandard2.0 works anywhere .NET Standard 2.0 is implemented.
cards/2/options/0: A contract: a list of APIs a platform must implement
cards/2/explain: You cannot run an app "on .NET Standard". You can only build a library for it.
cards/3/body:
2.0 (2017) is a huge set, more than 30,000 APIs. It is implemented by Framework 4.6.1+ (reliably from 4.7.2), .NET Core 2.0+, Mono and Unity.

2.1 (2019) added Span<T>, IAsyncEnumerable and default interface methods. It is implemented by .NET Core 3.0+ and Unity 2021.2+. .NET Framework does not implement it. Its ceiling is 2.0.
cards/4/task: A teammate built a shared library for netstandard2.1. Make it work in both Revit 2024 and Unity with a single target.
cards/5/q: Why did Framework never get .NET Standard 2.1?
cards/5/options/0: The new APIs need changes in the runtime itself, and Framework is frozen and updated in place
cards/5/options/2: The license did not allow it
cards/5/explain: Default interface methods, for example, need CLR support. Changing a CLR that all of Windows shares is too risky.
cards/6/task: Shared code for Unity, Revit 2025 and a .NET 10 app. You need Span<T> and IAsyncEnumerable without extra packages. One target.
cards/7/body:
There will be no .NET Standard after 2.1. Since .NET 5 there is just one platform, and a target like net8.0 or net10.0 means "everything in that version".

.NET Standard remains a bridge to Framework and Unity: 2.0 for maximum reach, 2.1 for Unity and modern .NET.
cards/8/q: Match each target to who can load it
cards/8/pairs/1/1: Unity and modern .NET, but not Framework
cards/9/q: What is true? Select all that apply.
cards/9/options/2: You can build an app for netstandard2.1 and run it
cards/9/options/3: There will be no new .NET Standard versions
cards/9/explain: Only libraries are built for .NET Standard.
